$comment: Session-describe reads the pinned upstream contract does not declare. The truth ratchet enforces manifest->code (a declared field's classification must be true); NOTHING enforced code->manifest, so a field we depend on but that the contract never declared was invisible — it simply arrived undefined and every guard built on it fell open in silence. That is how the pre-send context guard came to run permanently on its weak branch (live prod 2026-08-05: 200 consecutive decisions, fillSource always 'counter', while a turn died of context_length at a reported 51%). Enforced by describe-field-declaration.test.ts against the UNION of every name the pinned version declares (the session snapshot plus its TypeBox schemas): a read that is neither declared there nor listed here fails the suite. Listing one is a REVIEW EVENT, not a silencer — each entry must state what the code does when the field is absent, because that is the behaviour production actually gets.

estimatedPromptTokens.reason: Read at the TOP LEVEL of the session row, beside the nested read above, because the contract never said which shape the gateway uses and the two instructions in this repo disagree.
estimatedPromptTokens.whenAbsent: Nothing: the nested read is tried first and this only ever adds a second place to look. When both are absent the guard falls to the counter branch, as described for contextBudgetStatus.
estimatedPromptTokens.keepBecause: Looking in two places can only find more, never invent. Removing it before `/frame-discovery` settles the shape would be trading one guess for another.

promptBudgetBeforeReserve.reason: Same flat fallback as above — the denominator, i.e. the window minus the output reserve.
promptBudgetBeforeReserve.whenAbsent: The denominator falls back to the raw contextTokens. The two differ by the output reserve: the difference that makes a 96%-of-window session read comfortable while being at 117% of its real budget.

overflowTokens.reason: Same flat fallback — the gateway saying outright that the assembled prompt does not fit, the strongest signal the guard can act on.
overflowTokens.whenAbsent: The guard never sees a positive overflow, so its strongest escalation path is unreachable and it decides on the fill alone.

$resolved.contextBudgetStatus: DECLARED by the contract as of 2026.9.4 — removed from this allowlist on 2026-09-12, which is the outcome the entry was waiting for. It rode here since the pre-send guard existed because NO pinned version declared it (2026.6.11 through 2026.9.2), so its shape had been instructed twice from observation and the two readings disagreed. The vendored schema now answers that: the open `/frame-discovery contextBudgetStatus` question is no longer 'which shape does the gateway emit' but only whether it is omitted under a context engine that owns compaction. The flat sibling read (`estimatedPromptTokens`) stays listed: it is still undeclared, and it is still the second place the guard looks.
